record.paper_title: Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology
record.context_brief: t-equivalence of I and the Cantor set
record.original_question: With t-equivalence defined by homeomorphism of the function spaces C_p(X) and C_p(Y), is the unit interval I t-equivalent to the Cantor set?

evidence.quote:
Following it, we say that spaces X and Y are t-equivalent
if there exists a homeomorphism h of Cp(X) onto Cp(Y ).

Problem 19 (A. V. Arhangel’skii, ≤ 1989). Is the unit segment I t -equivalent to the
Cantor set?

artifact.self_contained_problem: For a Tychonoff topological space X, let C_p(X) denote the space of all continuous real-valued functions on X equipped with the topology of pointwise convergence (i.e., the subspace topology inherited from the product space R^X). Two Tychonoff spaces X and Y are said to be t-equivalent if C_p(X) and C_p(Y) are homeomorphic as topological spaces. Let I = [0,1] be the closed unit interval with its usual topology, and let K denote the standard middle-thirds Cantor set, regarded as a topological subspace of the real line. Determine whether I and K are t-equivalent; that is, decide whether C_p(I) and C_p(K) are homeomorphic.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not return clear evidence of a published resolution of this problem. It is recorded as a long-standing open problem attributed to A. V. Arhangel'skii (circa 1989), and no authoritative announcement of a solution was located.

status_evidence.title: Weak topology of an associated space and t-equivalence
status_evidence.snippet: Reference discussing t-equivalence in the setting of C_p(X), confirming the framework of the problem.
status_evidence.claim: The notion of t-equivalence via homeomorphism of C_p-spaces is an established but subtle equivalence relation, and questions distinguishing concrete compacta under it are known to be difficult.
